newsitem.title: UK: IGC trims estimate for world 1997/98 wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: IGC trims estimate for world 1997/98 wheat imports.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Thursday trimmed its estimate for world 1997/98 wheat imports by 400,000 tonnes to 93.2 million, after 91.3 million in 1996/97.
But the relatively slight alteration disguised major changes in the key consuming areas of the Middle East and Asia.

The IGC slashed its forecast for Chinese wheat imports by three million tonnes to four million, more in line with the 3.4 million forecast for 1996/97. Other reductions were seen for India and south Korea.
Industry sources noted that a good Chinese wheat crop had reduced the country's import demand.
"They have better production prospects -- last year it started this way. They have better estimates coming in all the time," said one.
Iran was expected to remain a major wheat importer in 1997/98, in fourth position in the world league table with an estimated 4.5 million tonnes.
This was 500,000 tonnes up on the IGC's estimate a month ago but still lower than the 5.7 million estimated for 1996/97.
The forecast for Middle East wheat imports was raised by 1.7 million tonnes, while that for Asia was cut by 4.4 million tonnes. All figures are based on calculations for the July/June crop year.
In Africa, the IGC's imports estimate rose by 1.3 million tonnes to 20.5 million after 18.1 in 1996/97.
The forecast for European imports was marginally higher at 4.1 million tonnes and slightly lower for the former Soviet Union at 3.4 million. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
